analysis:
Integration review of all 52 units found no concrete security regression. The PR rewrites Foundation Date `>=`/`<=` comparisons as `timeIntervalSince(_:) >= 0` or `<= 0`. It adds source and binary guards (scripts/check-date-comparisons.py, scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py) and documentation. Reasons: SDK 27.2 back-deploys those operators as weak imports, and pre-release macOS 27.2 crashes in a loop (an availability issue, relevant to A-018 and T-057).

Code changes verified from the supplied excerpts: AppAttestKeyHistoryBuilder.swift:50, AppAttestStallRestart.swift:130, EnrollmentKeyLifecycle.swift:6 (head line 6, `now.timeIntervalSince(allowed) >= 0`), ShadowEnrollmentAttempt.swift:20, ClusterModelProvisioningStore.swift (164, 193, 230) and ClusterService.swift (about 510, 646, 909, 1044, 1126). They keep the same operators and thresholds. For finite Dates they are equivalent, including equality. distantPast and distantFuture produce large finite intervals, so the behavior is unchanged. Per the unit 49 analysis, the stall-restart timestamp read rejects non-finite values (about line 146); I could not independently verify that line. They do not alter authorization, proof verification, the key-generation budget semantics (A-015/A-016), T-053 binding or revocation, the T-054 build qualification, or the manifest same-artifact, owner and atomic-write checks. The prefix cache posture (T-041) is untouched.

CI and workflow changes are additive: a release-lane-only step in .github/actions/provider-release-build/action.yml (head lines 354-367, set -euo pipefail, so a nonzero exit fails the build), a Release Integrity step in ci.yml (149-155), and path-filter additions in provider-release-cache.yml, release-dev-branch.yml and release-swift.yml. They add no secrets, permissions, network access, untrusted interpolation or unpinned actions. Docs and the threat-model header comment make claims that match the code.

Coverage limits: the scripts themselves, their tests and the ClusterService.swift line 1582 hunk (outside the supplied text) were not visible. The integration source replay is partial (198 of 384 units). Whether the weak-import checker fails closed on unexpected nm/otool output is unverified. This is a quality-gate effectiveness question, not a regression. No threat-model update is required beyond the existing header comment.
